image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, stands unhurried beside a whitewashed picket fence with a brush in hand, glancing sideways at a boy who watches him, in the summer heat of a dusty St. Petersburg street.

storyboard.claim: Tom reframes the whitewashing as a rare privilege, flipping work into play.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom painting slowly at the fence with a knowing sideways glance at an onlooker.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the fence scene: Tom has just decided the chore is a special honour.
storyboard.addedInformation: The attitude of the performance, not the labour itself, is what changes.

image.subject: Ben Rogers, a round-faced 12-year-old boy in a grey cotton shirt and frayed suspenders, hands his whole apple over to Tom Sawyer, a freckled boy in a faded blue shirt with bare feet, beside a whitewashed picket fence on a sunny street.

storyboard.claim: Ben is so captivated by the exclusivity that he gives away his apple for the chance to paint.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ben handing an apple across the fence to Tom, a cheerful, gullible grin on Ben's face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom has framed the chore as a privilege; Ben now pays for it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ben's crisp apple is the price of a turn at the brush.

image.subject: A tired clerk in a dark coat sits at a timber writing desk in a plain office, a ledger open and untouched, while a colleague across the room leans back idly looking busy with a pen.

storyboard.claim: Workplaces often reward the look of hard work over actual results.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clerk who looks busy at a desk with nothing much done.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from Tom's fence to the listener's own working life.
storyboard.addedInformation: Appearance-over-results is applied to a modern-feeling office in period dress.

image.subject: A plain white linen shirt laid folded on a polished shop counter in a mid-1840s store, beside a small gilt-edged card reading a price far above its worth.

storyboard.claim: A plain shirt sold at a huge price purely because of its label and status.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A plain white shirt on a counter with an inflated price card beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The listener's example of the fence logic applied to a shop.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shirt is the same as any other; only the label makes it precious.

storyboard.claim: The same dynamic is at work in a specific logo on a plain item.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; the sentence carries the idea alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Finishes the shop example in one line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the exact mechanism Twain is showing.

image.subject: A line of barefoot neighborhood boys waits along a whitewashed picket fence in the dusty sunlight, one of them holding a bright copper coin up toward the fence.

storyboard.claim: Value is driven entirely by perception and scarcity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A queue of boys eager for a turn at a fence, a coin held up.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Confirms the earlier point with the scene of the fence line forming.
storyboard.addedInformation: The queue shows scarcity turning into demand.

image.subject: An early-morning dusty board sidewalk in St. Petersburg, Missouri, with a whitewashed picket fence beside it, a tin bucket set down on the boards and long shadows in the heat.

storyboard.claim: Tom tests the market theory earlier that same morning, before Ben arrives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty morning street with a bucket and fence, a place of earlier experiment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Steps back in time from the fence to the morning scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: The setting of the earlier economic experiment.

image.subject: A young barefoot boy in a ragged shirt and patched trousers carries a tin bucket along a dusty street toward the town pump, his shoulders bent under the bucket's weight.

storyboard.claim: Jim is fetching water from the town pump, a task Tom normally hates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A barefoot boy walking with a heavy tin bucket toward the pump.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's earlier market test happens with this boy.
storyboard.addedInformation: The task is ordinary chore labour, carried by a child.

image.subject: A crowd of children gathered around an iron town pump on a dusty street in summer, some leaning on the post, some sitting on the edge of a trough, a few wrestling and laughing, buckets scattered.

storyboard.claim: The town pump is a busy social hub where children rest, trade and play.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A crowd of children loitering at an iron pump, idle and lively.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pump is where the boy with the bucket is headed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows why the water run takes an hour.

image.subject: Children sit and stand in a loose circle on a dusty sidewalk by the pump, trading small playthings in their palms, bartering with raised hands, and a scuffle breaks out at the edge.

storyboard.claim: Getting one bucket of water takes an hour because of all the socializing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Children trading toys in a circle by the pump.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the crowd at the pump into a trading scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: The delay is the social economy at work.

storyboard.claim: The water pump holds high social value, so Tom makes a trade there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a short confirmation line between the two speakers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A quick agreement that sets up Tom's offer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Clarifies the pump's value in the story's own terms.

image.subject: A small white glass alley marble resting in a boy's open palm on a dusty sidewalk, a tin bucket beside it, bright summer light across the boards.

storyboard.claim: Tom offers his favourite possession, a white marble, for Jim's labour.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A white marble on an open palm, held out as a trade.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pump's social market now gets a direct material offer.
storyboard.addedInformation: The marble is Tom's most treasured item, which makes the offer large.

image.subject: A barefoot boy in a ragged shirt stands by a tin bucket and a whitewash brush, hesitating and eyeing a marble held out to him, his face torn between temptation and doubt.

storyboard.claim: Jim is tempted by the marble and the sore toe, and almost accepts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy hesitating over a held-out marble with a brush in his other hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The offer is on the table; the boy is wavering.
storyboard.addedInformation: The almost-deal is the hook before the interruption.

image.subject: A stout, grey-haired woman of about sixty in a dark calico dress with a white collar and apron, spectacles on a cord, sweeping a slipper through the air from a doorway, a shocked boy ducking at the edge of a whitewashed fence.

storyboard.claim: Aunt Polly steps in with a flying slipper and ends the transaction before it happens.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly hurling a slipper from a doorway while the deal collapses.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The almost-deal is interrupted by the household authority.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows that direct trade is shut down by the town's authorities.

image.subject: A sunlit backyard of a timber house behind a whitewashed picket fence, the kitchen door standing open, a single worn slipper lying in the dirt.

storyboard.claim: Authorities can crush a direct trade whenever they choose to intervene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty yard after the slipper has been thrown, the door still open.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The slipper has landed; the market is shut down.
storyboard.addedInformation: The aftermath, not the violence, is shown.

storyboard.claim: Aunt Polly regulated Tom's business out of existence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a rhetorical question carries the beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the crackdown with a wry summary.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the outcome of the intervention.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer perched on the top rail of a whitewashed picket fence, chin in hand, a sly thoughtful look on his freckled face, the street quiet behind him.

storyboard.claim: After direct trade fails, Tom pivots to trading on psychology.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom sitting on a fence rail, thinking with a sly look.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The failed trade leads to a new plan.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's pivot is shown as a scheming pause.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer stands at a whitewashed picket fence in the afternoon sun, surrounded by a line of eager boys who hold out kites, marbles and bits of string as payment.

storyboard.claim: By the afternoon, Tom has turned the fence into a market and is rich.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom at the fence while boys queue up with things to trade.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The psychological pivot has worked; the market is open.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Tom at the centre of an economy.

image.subject: A homemade paper kite with a long string flying high over a dusty small-town street in Missouri, a summer sky behind it.

storyboard.claim: One of Tom's payments is a kite, traded for turns at the fence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A kite in a bright sky.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The first item in the list of payments.
storyboard.addedInformation: The kite is one of the goods Tom has collected.

image.subject: A dead grey rat hanging from a length of string tied to a picket fence rail, a broken piece of blue bottle glass lying on the dusty boards beside it.

storyboard.claim: Tom's collection includes a dead rat on a string and a blue bottle glass shard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A rat on a string and a blue glass shard on the boards.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the list of treasures Tom has collected.
storyboard.addedInformation: The absurd value of the items is shown directly.

storyboard.claim: Tom's haul is an entire economy of odd treasures.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; the list of items is the shape of the beat.
storyboard.onScreenText: KITE / DEAD RAT / 12 MARBLES / ONE-EYED KITTEN
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the list of payments from the afternoon market.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the full haul in one glance.

storyboard.claim: The objection: Tom is simply a lazy kid avoiding work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a real question is the point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A speaker challenges the praise of Tom's economics.
storyboard.addedInformation: Raises the counter-argument that Tom is just lazy.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled boy in a faded blue shirt and bare feet, leans back lazily against a whitewashed picket fence with a brush dangling from one hand, a half-smile on his face.

storyboard.claim: On the surface Tom looks like a lazy boy dodging labour.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom lounging on the fence with a brush dangling loosely.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question with the surface picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the slacker reading of the scene.

storyboard.claim: Calling Tom an economic genius gives a middle-school con artist too much credit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a one-line punchline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection gets its sharpest form.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the critique as a joke.

image.subject: A close view of a freckled boy's hands gripping a whitewash brush, the brush loaded and moving across a picket board, the effort visible in his shoulders.

storyboard.claim: A closer look at Tom's actual effort shows he works hard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hands on a brush working a board.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the objection toward the real effort.
storyboard.addedInformation: Work is visible, not idle.

image.subject: Ben Rogers, a round-faced boy in a grey cotton shirt and frayed suspenders, paints a picket fence with a whitewash brush while Tom Sawyer, in a faded blue shirt and bare feet, stands nearby watching him work.

storyboard.claim: Tom does not walk away once Ben takes the brush.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ben painting while Tom watches close by.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the effort point with a concrete scene of the handover.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom stays to supervise rather than leaving.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer sits on a wooden barrel in the shade of a tree beside a whitewashed fence, dangling his bare legs, munching an apple, his face relaxed and calculating.

storyboard.claim: Tom works twice as hard as manager of the operation than he would painting alone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom on a barrel in the shade with an apple.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The supervising Tom gets his own picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the management role and his apple.

image.subject: From behind, a freckled boy sits on a barrel in the shade, bare legs swinging, an apple in one hand, looking out over a row of other boys at a fence in the sun.

storyboard.claim: Tom sits in the shade actively planning more exploitation of innocence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy on a barrel looking over a line of boys at the fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the barrel scene with the planning.
storyboard.addedInformation: The planning is seen in the watchful pose.

storyboard.claim: Tom must maintain the illusion of exclusivity for hours.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; the sentence carries the idea alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the curation of the vibe.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the duration of the performance.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer leans against a picket fence with his arms folded and a feigned look of reluctance, while a new boy approaches holding out a kite and a dead rat on a string to bargain.

storyboard.claim: Each new boy triggers the same performance of reluctance and bargaining.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom reluctant at the fence as a new boy approaches with goods.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The barrel scene shows how the routine repeats for each newcomer.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bargaining goods are named visually.

image.subject: A busy stretch of whitewashed fence on a dusty street, several barefoot boys handing over kites, string, tickets and small glass bottles to each other in the afternoon sun.

storyboard.claim: Tom works tirelessly to sustain a functioning economy out of thin air.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boys trading goods along a busy fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The routine now shown as an active market.
storyboard.addedInformation: The economy is shown as busy and self-sustaining.

storyboard.claim: John Cely calls Tom an actor manager staging a production.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a quotation carries the beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A critic's reading of the performance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the critic's frame: Tom is a manager, not lazy.

image.subject: A small stack of hand-lettered paper tickets tied with string on a whitewashed fence rail, a boy's hand reaching to take one in the bright afternoon sun.

storyboard.claim: Tom literally printed his own currency in the form of tickets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A stack of paper tickets on a fence rail.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The performance now becomes a currency.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tickets are the currency Tom invented.

storyboard.claim: This brings the argument back to its core thesis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; a short bridge line.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ties the currency back to the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the turn toward the general claim.

image.subject: A knot of townspeople in plain summer clothes talk together in a dusty street in small groups, heads leaning in, the heat shimmering above the boards.

storyboard.claim: Value is just a community agreement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townspeople gathered in small groups in the street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The thesis now gets a town-wide picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: The agreement is a crowd of people, not a single person.

image.subject: Four eager neighborhood boys stand along a whitewashed picket fence, one holding a paintbrush out to another, all of them looking keen and envious in the summer heat.

storyboard.claim: Tom convinces the town to value a punishment as a privilege.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Boys eager to paint the fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The agreement is shown in the eagerness of the boys.
storyboard.addedInformation: The punishment is now a sought-after privilege.

storyboard.claim: They agreed the fence was fun, so it became fun.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No picture; the statement carries the idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the agreement point with a short line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fun is shown as a shared decision.

image.subject: A dusty road in a small Missouri town on a summer morning, townsfolk in dark Sunday clothes walking toward a small plain wooden church.

storyboard.claim: Tom takes his newly acquired capital to the town's most rigid institution, the Sunday school.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townsfolk in Sunday clothes walking to church.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fence economy now moves toward the church.
storyboard.addedInformation: The setting shifts from fence to church.

image.subject: A Sunday school room with rows of wooden benches, a lectern with a Bible on it, bright windows and the faint smell of wax in the light.

storyboard.claim: The church is the next place to test the economy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Sunday school room with benches and a lectern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Enters the church the previous beat named.
storyboard.addedInformation: The room is the stage for the next sequence.

image.subject: A small, plain white wooden church in a Missouri river town with a pine-board box for a steeple on its roof, under a bright summer sky.

storyboard.claim: The Sunday school building is small, plain and austere.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Exterior of a plain wooden church with a box steeple.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The camera moves from the street to the building.
storyboard.addedInformation: The building's austerity sets up its rigid rules.
